metadata.title: IREN delivers first 50MW Microsoft AI cloud deployment at Childress

content.text:
IREN (NASDAQ: IREN) said Thursday that Microsoft accepted Horizon 1, a 50MW critical IT load AI cloud deployment at its Childress, Texas, campus.
Four 50MW deployments are due in 2026 under IREN's five-year, $9.7 billion cloud services contract with Microsoft, with Horizon 1 the first. The completed build uses direct-to-chip liquid cooling and NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems.
IREN also received NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud status after NVIDIA tested the Horizon 1 deployment. IREN said the designation reflects the system's performance and reliability on AI workloads.

The four Microsoft deployments, named Horizons 1 through 4, will provide a combined 200MW of critical IT load when completed. IREN expects to deliver the remaining three phases later this year.
"Delivering Horizon 1 demonstrates the strength of our vertically integrated model and our ability to execute complex AI infrastructure projects at speed and scale," IREN co-founder and co-CEO Daniel Roberts said. Roberts said more than 3,000 people across the site team contributed to the delivery.
The Microsoft agreement was announced by IREN in November 2025 and includes a 20% customer prepayment. Once fully commissioned, the contract is expected to generate about $1.94 billion in annualized run-rate revenue; IREN also agreed to buy approximately $5.8 billion of GPUs and related equipment from Dell.
IREN closed a $3.65 billion financing package in June to support the Microsoft buildout. The package comprised a $2.10 billion private placement whose fixed pricing equated to SOFR plus 213 bps, along with a $1.55 billion delayed-draw term loan at SOFR plus 225 bps. IREN reported a 6% blended cost of debt after hedging the floating-rate portion.
The Microsoft delivery follows IREN's $2.8 billion of additional AI cloud contracts announced in July. Those agreements lifted the year-end 2026 target for annualized run-rate revenue from $3.7 billion to more than $4 billion, with about 85% of the revised target under contract.

For 2026, IREN continues to target 480MW of gross AI cloud capacity, followed by 1.2GW in 2027. Those figures are expansion targets and include infrastructure beyond the 200MW of critical IT load contracted by Microsoft at Childress.
